cards.explanation: The answer is that they want to see Jesus, friends. The Greeks, some visitors who came up to worship at the feast, tell Philip, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.” (John 12:21) No speech and no warm-up. My own requests come with a ten minute introduction, so I admire this.

The answer is True, friends. Philip tells Andrew, and then the text says both of them went and told Jesus (John 12:22). Philip, Andrew, one message, and they walk in together. Nobody has to carry that news alone.

The answer is that it dies, friends. Jesus says, “…unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a seed. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.” (John 12:24) It sounds backwards, doesn't it? The seed that seems to be lost is the one that bears the fruit.

The answer is False, friends. Jesus says, “Whoever loves his life will lose it, but whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.” (John 12:25) So loving your life is the one that loses it. It's a flip from what most of us expect, and I had to read it twice myself.

The word is follow, friends. Jesus says, “If anyone serves Me, he must follow Me; and where I am, My servant will be as well.” (John 12:26) Serving and following go together here. Where He is, His servant will be too.
The answer is the Father, friends. Jesus says, “If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.” (John 12:26) The honor comes from the Father Himself. No applause machine needed.
The answer is troubled, friends. Jesus says, “Now My soul is troubled…” (John 12:27) I think this is a heavy moment, so I'll leave it there with Him. He says it plainly and the text doesn't hide it.

The answer is False, friends. Jesus asks, “‘Father, save Me from this hour’?” and then says, “No, it is for this purpose that I have come to this hour.” (John 12:27) The question is there, but the request never comes. What He asks instead is, “Father, glorify Your name!” (John 12:28)

The answer is that a voice comes from heaven, friends. Right after Jesus says, “Father, glorify Your name!” a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.” (John 12:28) It's an answer to His prayer. And the crowd standing there can hear it.

The answer is an angel, friends. Some said it had thundered, and others said that an angel had spoken to Him (John 12:29). Same sound, two different answers. A crowd can hear the very same thing and still say different things about it.
The answer is False, friends. Jesus says, “This voice was not for My benefit, but yours.” (John 12:30) The voice was for the crowd. They were the ones standing there when it came, and they heard it.

The answer is that He will draw everyone to Himself, friends. Jesus says, “And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to Myself.” (John 12:32) Everyone is a big word, and He uses it. Notice that it's Him doing the drawing.

The answer is True, friends. The writer says, “He said this to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.” (John 12:33) So being lifted up points to how He would die. The writer tells us so plainly.

The answer is that they ask who this Son of Man is, friends. The crowd asks, “Who is this Son of Man?” (John 12:34) They already have the Law in their heads, so now they want to know who He's talking about. It's a fair question to ask.

The word is darkness, friends. Jesus says, “Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you.” (John 12:35) The Light is among them for a little while longer. The call is to walk while it's there.

The answer is False, friends. Jesus says, “While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light.” (John 12:36) The word is while. He doesn't say to wait for it to come back.

The answer is sons of light, friends. Jesus says, “While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light.” (John 12:36) Believing in the Light is how they may become sons of light. It's an invitation, and it's open right then.

The answer is that He goes away and is hidden from them, friends. The text says, “After Jesus had spoken these things, He went away and was hidden from them.” (John 12:36) He finishes what He has to say, and then He's gone from their sight. The story isn't over, friends.
